newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Stork says could take part in Fokker restart.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Stork says could take part in Fokker restart.

text.p: Dutch industrial group Stork, which in July acquired the profitable maintenance activities of bankrupt planemaker Fokker, said on Tuesday it was prepared to take a minority stake in a re-started company.
"We have said we are prepared to take a minority stake in a restart construction provided it is with a strong partner," said Stork spokesman Koos Huurdeman.

As buyer of Fokker Aviation, the planemaker's maintenance and product support arm, Stork has been involved in the recent talks on a possible takeover of the planemaking activities by South Korea's Samsung Aerospace.

As a result Stork had also been able to make an assessment of the Samsung bid, Huurdeman said, but declined to comment whether the South Koreans were seen by Stork as the strong partner it was demanding.
Stork's Fokker Aviation buy was conditional on the division being sold back should Stork prove unwilling or unable to cooperate with a future buyer of the planemaking activities.
"We are certainly not standing in the way of a restart (for the plane-making activities) -- it's not in our interests," Huurdeman said.
"As things stand, we are maintaining a finite fleet...in the event of a restart this could in principle become infinite."
Fokker's receivers said on Monday they hoped for news on the company's possible takeover some time on Tuesday.
Fokker's suppliers have set November 1 as a final deadline before they start closing down production lines, which would make the planemaker's bankruptcy irreversible.
-- Lien van der Leij Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
